title: Section 165 — Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master

content.overview: BNS s. 165 — Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master. Historical concordance: IPC 137. For conduct governed by the BNS, cite BNS section 165; the IPC reference is historical concordance.
In student language: BNS s. 165 is the rule on “Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master”. The section provides that the master or person in charge of a merchant vessel, on board of which any deserter from the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India is concealed, shall, though ignorant of such concealment, be liable to a penalty not exceeding three thousand rupees, if he might have known of such concealment but for some neglect of his duty as such master or person in charge, or but for some want of discipline on board of the vessel. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 165 exists so that “Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master” has a closed legal test in Chapter VIII — Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Mutiny, desertion, insubordination, and wearing a service garb.

The provision in detail
165. The master or person in charge of a merchant vessel, on board of which any deserter from the Army, Navy or Air Force of the Government of India is concealed, shall, though ignorant of such concealment, be liable to a penalty not exceeding three thousand rupees, if he might have known of such concealment but for some neglect of his duty as such master or person in charge, or but for some want of discipline on board of the vessel

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 165 (Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master), Chapter VIII — Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 165 constitutes a key component of Chapter VIII (Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master under Section 165 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 165.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 165 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 165 vs General Attempt: Section 165 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter VIII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 165 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 165 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused is liable under BNS s. 165 for conduct relating to deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master.
Rule: Under BNS s. 165, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 165.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 165 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
